title: Folders
description:
One folder and the folders directly inside it, as a front end may offer
them to be chosen.

failures.description:
What it could not read or name, each with its code
([`BrowseFailure`]): a subfolder whose type will not read, or whose
path no request could send back, a hidden one only when hidden
ones are asked for.

folders.description:
Its subfolders, in the order of their names, hidden ones only when
asked for, and no more than [`FOLDERS_CAP`].

hidden.description:
How many of its subfolders are hidden, their names starting with a
`.`, listed or not: what asking for them would list, the bound
aside.

home.description:
The home the front end was given, normalized, as a folder a request
may name, for a way back to it: none when there is none, or when it
is no such path ([`policy::path`]).

is.description: What it is itself, so it can be chosen as one of its subfolders can.

path.description: The folder listed, absolute, as it was asked for.

trail.description:
Each folder from the root down to it, it last: what a front end
offers to go up by, each by the path it is asked for by.

truncated.description:
Whether it holds more subfolders than [`FOLDERS_CAP`], which
`folders` stops at.

Crumb.description: One folder on the way down to the one listed.

name.description: Its name, or the root's path for the root, which has none.

Folder.description: One folder directly inside the one listed.

linked.description:
Whether the workspace links it, by the path an entry leads to, as
`mindweaver link` would tell.

path.description: Where it is, absolute, as a request names it to list it in turn.

symlink.description:
Whether it is a link to a folder rather than a folder: listed and
opened as one all the same.

FolderIs.description:
What a folder is, the strongest of what it holds: a mind project, a
flayer workspace, a git repository, or any other folder.

Said.description:
An error as a serialized type holds one: its code, for a front end to act
on, and its message, for whoever reads it.

Built where the type is serialized, or kept in what a front end reads
(the workspace's snapshot), in place of the error, since an error
holds what JSON has no shape for (an `io::Error`, a parser's own), and
only these two are meant to leave core. Its fields are public for a
front end that reads the snapshot as Rust rather than as JSON, the TUI.

message.description:
Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as every URL
is: an error can quote one, a source's among them, and what built
the error is no promise that it carries no credential.
